case.title: Epileptic spasms and developmental regression
case.brief:
Referral from paediatric neurology. A girl developed normally until 7 months, when epileptic spasms began with hypsarrhythmia on her EEG. She has lost skills and has axial hypotonia. Her MRI is normal. She is now 14 months old and still has spasms despite vigabatrin and prednisolone.

Trio exome sequencing, analysed with the epilepsy panel, found a heterozygous SCN2A variant, NM_001040142.2:c.2558G>A p.(Arg853Gln), which neither parent carries. The exome confirms that both parents are her biological parents.
tasks: Score the de novo evidence with ClinGen’s points, counting this patient and any others you find in ClinVar and the literature. Is it PS2 or PM6, and at what strength?
Compare the missense predictors with their calibrated thresholds. What strength of PP3 do the ACGS and ClinGen allow?
Look at the protein: where is the variant, and are pathogenic missense variants clustered there?
Classify the variant and sign it, then compare with the ClinGen Epilepsy Sodium Channel expert panel.
case.source: The variant is NM_001040142.2(SCN2A):c.2558G>A (GRCh38 2-165342465-G-A, ClinGen allele CA210022), and it is absent from gnomAD v4.1. The sources are ClinVar VCV000194555 and the ClinGen Epilepsy Sodium Channel VCEP’s classification in the Evidence Repository, checked in October 2026. The patient and family are fictional.

patients.ref: Case 5: an infant with epileptic spasms and developmental regression
patients.referral: Paediatric neurology referred her because of epileptic spasms with hypsarrhythmia from 7 months and a loss of skills.
patients.summary: She is 14 months old and developed normally until 7 months, when epileptic spasms began and her EEG showed hypsarrhythmia. She has since lost her smile and her interest in toys, and she has axial hypotonia. Her brain MRI is normal. The spasms continue despite vigabatrin and prednisolone.
patients.familyHistory: Her parents are unrelated and well, and so is her older brother. There is no family history of epilepsy.
patients.notes: The patient and family are fictional, but the variant and the published evidence about it are real.

expected.source: ClinGen Epilepsy Sodium Channel expert panel (VCEP), Evidence Repository, specifications v1.0.0; ClinVar VCV000194555 (Pathogenic, reviewed by expert panel, 2023-05-09).

notes.PS2: Met, because the variant has been found de novo, with maternity and paternity confirmed, in at least four published people with consistent phenotypes. This patient is another, since the trio exome confirms her parentage. Under the panel’s current specification (v2.0), each such person with a complex neurodevelopmental disorder scores 1 point. A total of 2 points is strong, and 4 is very strong.
notes.PS3: Met, because patch-clamp studies show that the peak sodium current is 51% of normal.
notes.PM1: Met at moderate strength, which is the only strength the panel uses for PM1. The residue lies in one of the pathogenic-enriched regions of the channel that the panel lists in its PM1 table.
notes.PM2: Met at supporting strength, because the variant is absent from gnomAD v4.1, as it was from v2.1.1 when the panel curated it.
notes.PP3: Met at moderate strength. A REVEL score of 0.95 would reach strong by ClinGen’s calibration, whose threshold is 0.932 (Pejaver et al. 2022), but the panel caps PP3 at moderate. It also caps PM1 and PP3 together at strong. The ACGS 2024 guidelines would use PP3 at supporting strength only.
